To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gross calorific value of longleaf pine was not impacted by the presence of extractives and that IR spectroscopy coupled with partial least squares regression can be used to predict gross calorific value with reasonable accuracy.
the GCV of longleaf pine wood chips can be accurately predicted using NIR spectroscopy, and that the GCV is affected by extractives content.
the gross heat of combustion of longleaf pine was not affected by extractives content, and that infrared (IR) and multivariate analysis can be used to predict the gross heat of calorific value.

the following questions.
the determination of the GCG and extractives content of longleaf pine, and the development of a rapid method to determine these properties.
the determination of GCV in longleaf pine using IR spectroscopy and multivariat analysis, and the investigation of the impact of extractives on GCV.

this study demonstrates that there is a measurable impact of extractives on GCV in longleaf pine, and that the IR spectroscopic approach can be used to predict GCV with reasonable accuracy.
